steps.name: QC and paired DESeq2 differential expression
caveats: Must use the paired design (~subject + condition), not a naive two-group unpaired test, since each subject contributes both a control and treated sample
Confirm metadata subject/condition columns map correctly to count matrix column names before fitting the model
With n=5 pairs, power is limited; report this explicitly rather than overinterpreting borderline p-values
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control blood samples, controlling for the 5-subject pairing (paired design ~subject + condition)?
acceptance_criteria: counts.csv (12000 genes x 10 samples) and metadata.csv (10 rows: subject, condition) are loaded and sample order/names are matched/verified between the two files
Low-count genes are filtered (e.g., require count >=10 in at least 5 samples) before DE testing
DESeq2 is run with design ~subject + condition (paired/blocked design), with condition releveled so 'treated vs control' is the tested contrast
Output table includes gene, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj for all tested genes, ranked by padj
A results summary reports number of significant genes at padj<0.05 and describes any that don't have complete pairs

steps.name: Per-subject response consistency of DE genes
caveats: Use DESeq2 normalized (size-factor corrected) counts, not raw counts, when computing per-subject fold-changes
With only 5 subjects, concordance metrics are descriptive, not a formal statistical test — do not present them as p-values
steps.question: Among genes identified as differentially expressed (paired DESeq2 in T1S1), how consistent is the treated-vs-control response across each of the 5 individual subjects?
acceptance_criteria: For each of the top DE genes (e.g., padj<0.05, or top 50 by padj if none pass threshold), compute the per-subject log2(treated/control) using normalized counts (pseudocount added)
Produce a subject x gene matrix of per-subject fold-changes and summarize concordance (e.g., fraction of subjects with same-direction change, coefficient of variation across subjects)
Flag genes whose significant group-level effect is driven by one or two subjects rather than a consistent response across all 5
Output a table of per-subject fold-changes for top DE genes plus a concordance summary metric per gene

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treatment-responsive genes
caveats: With only 12000 genes profiled and n=5 pairs, the DE gene list feeding enrichment may be short; report enrichment results as exploratory given limited input list size
Use the WikiPathways human (HGNC symbol) gene sets specifically — do not substitute the mouse or rat WikiPathways files present in the reference store
steps.question: Which biological pathways are over-represented among genes that respond to treatment (from the paired DESeq2 contrast in T1S1)?
acceptance_criteria: Check that the WikiPathways human GMT reference is present before running; if absent, report enrichment step skipped and why

Run over-representation or GSEA-style enrichment using the ranked/significant gene list from T1S1 (padj<0.05, or top N ranked by padj/log2FC if none pass threshold) against WikiPathways human gene sets
Report enriched pathways with adjusted p-values (e.g., BH-corrected) and the overlapping gene symbols per pathway
State explicitly if gene symbol matching between the count matrix and the WikiPathways gene sets required any normalization (case, aliasing)

plan.title: Paired control-vs-treated DE analysis, 5 subjects
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are raw STAR/featureCounts gene-level integer counts for 12000 genes across 10 samples (5 subjects, each with a matched control and treated blood sample), a paired within-subject design. The correct model uses a paired/blocked DESeq2 design (~subject + condition) so that per-subject baseline expression differences are removed and the treatment effect is estimated from within-subject control-vs-treated contrasts, matching the biological question 'which genes respond to treatment within each subject'. After QC and DE, treatment-responsive genes are also examined per-subject (log2FC consistency across the 5 paired differences) to characterize how uniform vs heterogeneous the subject-level response is, then pathway enrichment (WikiPathways human) contextualizes the gene-level findings.
